title: Recipes from the River: Cucumber & Red Onion Salad with Black Vinegar and Dill
contentHtml:
This light, sweet, and vinegary side salad is perfect to accompany a rich main course. And it's especially refreshing after a long day on the river!

The second night of our trip—as documented in our Cooking on the River series—starred rich, creamy, warming Stir-Fried Shrimp & Grits, inspired by both Southern and Sichuan flavors. That left the side salads to help cut through the heartiness of our main course. We served this light Cucumber & Red Onion Salad alongside Braised Green Beans with Pickled Mustard Greens (recipe coming later this week).

This salad comes together quickly and heavily utilizes pantry staples. And we might be biased, but after a long day taking on the whitewater rapids of the Colorado River, few things felt more refreshing than this dish. Luckily, you don't need to pack up a mega-raft to enjoy this one for yourself.

Every recipe I publish here is personally tested, tasted, and approved.

Serves: 6

Ingredients

  • 2 pounds English, Persian, or Japanese cucumbers, peeled, seeded, and cut into large bite-sized chunks

  • ½ large red onion, very thinly sliced

  • ½ bunch dill, roughly chopped

  • ⅓ cup Chinkiang black vinegar

  • 3 tablespoons cider vinegar

  • 3 tablespoons sugar

  • 1 ½ tablespoons neutral oil

  • Kosher salt

  • Freshly ground black pepper

Method

  1. Toss the cucumbers. With onion and salt, toss cucumbers. Rest 10 to 15 minutes, then drain excess liquid.

  2. Mix and serve. In a large salad bowl, whisk together the black vinegar, cider vinegar, sugar, and oil. Season with salt and black pepper. Add the cucumbers, onion, and dill and toss just before serving
